source.title: Modern Release Engineering in a Nutshell -- Why Researchers should Care
source.venue: IEEE 23rd International Conference on Software Analysis, Evolution, and Reengineering (SANER 2016), Future of Software Engineering track, pp. 78-90

confidence_rationale: Peer-reviewed invited overview of modern release-engineering practice; good source quality but broad rather than empirical on the specific event-definition question. It supports treating a version boundary as a discrete, decided pipeline milestone (mapping well to governance_acceptance) but its emphasis on AUTOMATED, objective pipeline gates is a mild counter-current to a human governance sign-off, so it is supporting-with-a-caveat rather than clean support. Mapping fidelity moderate and weighted heavily.
failure_signatures: The paper's trajectory is toward automated, tool-enforced release gates (CI, build, deploy, infrastructure-as-code), which is closer to Q-087's rejected strict-green-board (objective/automatic) than to its chosen governance-acceptance (human decision) -- so it partly cuts against the resolution it otherwise supports.

It concerns the release cadence of continuously-deployed products, not the one-time freezing of a research substrate as a causal reference; 'release' there recurs, whereas V3 closure is a singular boundary.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Release engineering 'encompasses code change integration, continuous integration, build system specifications, infrastructure-as-code, deployment and release,' and modern continuous-delivery practices 'bring new content to the end user in days or hours rather than months or years' -- framing release as a defined, repeatedly-triggered stage of an explicit engineering pipeline.
mapping.ree_translation: In modern practice a version/release boundary is a discrete milestone that a team explicitly triggers within a defined process, not the passive point at which a system becomes provably complete. This supports Q-087's resolution that V3 closure be a declared governance event recorded on a controllable date (governance_acceptance) rather than an emergent all-green state.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper trends toward automated, objective pipeline gates, which resembles Q-087's REJECTED strict-green-board candidate more than its chosen human governance-acceptance; the support is therefore for 'closure is a decided milestone,' not for 'the decider should be a human governance judgement.' It also addresses recurring product releases, not a singular research-substrate freeze, so the analogy to a one-time closure event is loose.
mapping.source_context: Software release engineering; invited Future-of-Software-Engineering overview of the modern continuous-delivery pipeline and its research implications.

confidence_components.notes: Peer-reviewed but a broad overview, not a study of the release-decision event specifically. Mapping fidelity moderate: 'release as a decided pipeline milestone' transfers, but the automation emphasis pulls toward the rejected objective-gate candidate. Transfer risk moderate: deployed-product release cadence -> singular substrate-freeze governance event.
